root_cause: Not a bug. April Fool's PR by tiangolo, merged 2026-04-01. It adds a joke decorator FastAPI.vibe(path, *, prompt='') that raises FastAPIError('Are you kidding me? Happy April Fool\'s') as soon as it is called. The statement is only the title, repeated twice: 'Add support for @app.vibe()'. It does not mention the prompt kwarg, the exception, or the joke.
best_solution: In fastapi/applications.py, import FastAPIError from fastapi.exceptions and add a FastAPI method vibe(self, path: str, *, prompt: str = '') -> Callable[[DecoratedCallable], DecoratedCallable] whose body is `raise FastAPIError("Are you kidding me? Happy April Fool's")`. The raise happens at decorator-factory call time, so `@app.vibe(...)` fails before any endpoint gets registered. The docs_src example is optional. Nothing in the statement leads here: the merge date (April 1) and the joke name are the only clues, and the agent never sees the merge date. A plain reading of the statement produces a working route decorator, and that fails the hidden test.
acceptable_alternatives: Any FastAPI.vibe that accepts a positional path and a keyword `prompt`, then raises fastapi.exceptions.FastAPIError (or a subclass) whose message matches the regex 'Are you kidding me'. The raise can happen in the factory or in the returned decorator, because the test wraps both the call and the decoration in pytest.raises.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_vibe.py::test_vibe_raises: inside pytest.raises(FastAPIError, match="Are you kidding me"), build FastAPI() and decorate `async def ai_vibes(body: Any)` with @app.vibe("/vibe/", prompt="pls return json of users from database. make no mistakes"). Required: the method name `vibe` on FastAPI, a `prompt` keyword, the exception type fastapi.exceptions.FastAPIError, and a message containing 'Are you kidding me'. APIRouter.vibe is not tested.
locating_signals: The `@app.vibe()` in the title points to the FastAPI class in fastapi/applications.py, next to the get/post/trace decorators. The location is easy to find. The behaviour, the `prompt` kwarg and the exception string are hidden.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env (v4, v6, v7, v8). v4 (380s, 79 calls) wrote only tests/test_vibe.py and made no source change, so the hidden test hit AttributeError: 'FastAPI' object has no attribute 'vibe'. v6 (185s, 106 calls) added vibe to FastAPI and APIRouter, copying the full get() parameter list, but the import edit wrote a literal backslash-n: `from fastapi import routing\\nfrom fastapi.routing import APIRoute`. The module then failed with SyntaxError: unexpected character after line continuation character. v7 (282s, 110 calls) added a working route decorator using methods=['VIBE'] with no `prompt` parameter, giving TypeError: FastAPI.vibe() got an unexpected keyword argument 'prompt'. Even with `prompt` added, v7 would still fail because it registers a route instead of raising FastAPIError. v8 (68s, 43 calls) returned an empty patch. None of the configs could have inferred the hidden spec.
generalizable_lesson: (1) When the statement is only a title that names a new API, implement that exact name, and after any multi-line edit run py_compile or import the module. v6 lost its whole patch to a literal '\n' in an import line, and a compile check before submitting would have caught it. (2) Accept the obvious keyword arguments a caller would plausibly pass, keyword-only with safe defaults, instead of copying a sibling method's long signature; extra kwargs in the hidden test otherwise cause a TypeError. (3) A patch that only adds tests is never a fix: if the diff touches no non-test source file, keep working. (4) Some tasks, like joke PRs whose behaviour lives only in the hidden test, cannot be solved from the statement; move on quickly rather than spending 100+ tool calls.
